result:
Both integrate changes from one branch into another, but merge preserves history as it happened while rebase rewrites it to be linear.

`git merge feature` ties the two branches together with a new merge commit that has both as parents, leaving every existing commit untouched. `git rebase main` (run from your feature branch) replays your commits one by one on top of main's tip, creating new commits with new hashes, so the result looks as if you had started your work from the latest main.

In practice, rebase to tidy up a local branch that only you have, and merge to bring finished work into a shared branch. Don't rebase commits that others have already pulled: their history will diverge from yours and you'll have to force-push, which can clobber their work. Conflicts also differ: merge asks you to resolve them once, whereas rebase may stop at each replayed commit.
